title: Compact snapshot streaming and local TTL index proxy for tenant dashboard pagination
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Background:
The console dashboard experiences intermittent 95th/99th percentile tail latency when users paginate across large time windows (30d+) or request wide page sizes (>=50 rows). Current contributors: scatter-read amplification across time-partitioned materialized views, stale KV cache misses for tenant-specific filters, and synchronous MV reads that block streaming results.

Goal:
Ship a low-risk change that reduces tail latency for common dashboard paging patterns by improving read locality and enabling fast streaming of compact snapshots while preserving correctness and pagination semantics. Target: 95th percentile endpoint latency <150ms for page_size=50 on typical tenant workloads and 3× reduction in read amplification for multi-partition scans.

Proposal (high level):
1) Compact snapshot streaming: produce a compact, read-optimized snapshot of the query result set on the query-coordinator layer, streamed to the client as a page-backed cursor. Snapshots are serialized as a compact columnar segment (protobuf) that references lightweight row pointers into materialized views; first page is streamed immediately while remaining pages are served from the snapshot cache.
2) Local TTL index proxy: introduce a per-coordinator in-memory index proxy that maintains Bloom-hinted, time-partition-aware lightweight indexes with short TTL (default 60s). The proxy coalesces concurrent range lookups into a single MV read and serves subsequent pagination requests with drastically fewer MV calls.
3) Memtable coalescing: for hot tenants, coalesce small write deltas into a compact memtable view used by the snapshoter to avoid repeated reads of many small segments.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Correctness: snapshots maintain deterministic pagination by anchoring to a server-side stable continuation token. We accept eventual snapshot staleness between pages (same semantics as a point-in-time snapshot) — documented to frontend teams.
- Memory vs latency: TTL index proxy keeps per-tenant index state; to bound memory we shard index proxy by tenant weight and evict by LRU + estimated query cost. This favors low-latency for top tenants at the expense of cold-read performance for low-usage tenants.
- Rollout complexity: initial rollout will be coordinator-side only, behind a feature flag and a per-route sampling rate to collect correctness and performance telemetry.

Implementation plan (major tasks):
- Build snapshot serializer/deserializer and streaming API (server-side streaming + client cursor patch).
- Implement TTL index proxy with Bloom hints and coalescing logic.
- Add memtable coalescer for hot-tenant delta folding.
- Integrate with existing pagination contract and generate server-side continuation tokens.
- Instrument: telemetry for MV read amplification, snapshot cache hit rate, 50/95/99 latency, memory usage per proxy shard.
- Create migration plan: start sampling 2% of queries, then 10%, 25% with monitoring gates.

Acceptance criteria and metrics (will be validated during rollout):
- 95th percentile latency for sampled dashboard pagination queries (page_size=50, time_window=30d) improves to <150ms in the sampled population.
- MV read amplification reduced by >=3x for sampled tenants.
- Snapshot cache hit rate >= 60% at 10% sampling for top 50 tenants.
- No regressions in correctness: pagination sequences produce stable deterministic result sets for the snapshoted session.
- Memory overhead per coordinator shard stays below configured budget (default 8GB).

Test plan:
- Unit tests for serializer, token semantics, and index proxy correctness.
- Integration tests using synthetic tenants with controlled partition cardinality and write churn to validate cache eviction and coalescing behavior.
- Load test in staging reproducing tail latency scenarios; compare baseline vs feature-flag enabled runs.
- Canary rollout with observability dashboards and automated rollback triggers (latency above threshold or error rate > baseline+0.5%).

Rollout and monitoring dashboards (initial):
- Endpoint: /internal/metrics/console-pagination/sampled
- Charts: MV read calls per query, snapshot cache hit rate, per-tenant memory footprint, latency p50/p95/p99, streaming throughput (rows/sec)
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency <150ms for sampled page_size=50 queries
MV read amplification reduced by >=3x in sampled runs
Snapshot cache hit rate >=60% at 10% sampling for top 50 tenants
Deterministic pagination preserved across snapshot sessions
Memory overhead per coordinator shard within configured budget

2025-02-26 Marco D. Reyes: Prototype of compact serializer done (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2148). Local microbenchmarks show 2.4× speedup for first-page serializing vs baseline.
2025-03-01 QA: Integration test case added for cursor determinism across snapshot boundaries. Found edge case when partition compaction overlaps snapshot window — patch uploaded.
2025-03-04 Aisha K. Patel: Updated rollout to phased sampling and added automated rollback gates. Planning canary start 2025-03-10 behind feature flag f_snapstream.
